overview: The two major arms of the immune system, distinguished by speed, specificity, and whether they remember past encounters.
genZNote: Innate: the bouncer at the door, no questions asked. Adaptive: intelligence agency that remembers your face forever.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The immune system's rapid, non-specific first line of defense, present from birth.
aspects.valueB: The immune system's slower, highly specific response that improves with repeated exposure to a pathogen.

aspects.label: Speed of Response
aspects.valueB: Days to develop initially, but much faster on re-exposure due to memory.

aspects.label: Specificity
aspects.valueA: Recognizes broad, shared molecular patterns (PAMPs) via pattern recognition receptors.
aspects.valueB: Recognizes specific antigens via highly diverse B-cell and T-cell receptors.

aspects.label: Immunological Memory
aspects.valueA: No memory — responds the same way every time.
aspects.valueB: Generates memory B and T cells for faster, stronger responses upon re-exposure.

aspects.label: Key Cellular/Molecular Components
aspects.valueA: Neutrophils, macrophages, natural killer cells, complement system, physical barriers.
aspects.valueB: B lymphocytes, T lymphocytes, antibodies, and antigen-presenting cells that bridge to innate immunity.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Slower initially, highly specific, generates memory.
